data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy governing the use of information technology (IT) cost estimating key principles and uniform best practice guidance for all major and non-major USDA IT investments, projects, or systems.
policy_statements.target: all major and non-major USDA IT investments, projects, or systems

policy_statements.source_text: This DR incorporates leading practices that create a “forcing function” of tasks, activities, or events that will drive the USDA to take action and produce a unified set of IT cost estimating activities and results.
policy_statements.target: leading practices that create a “forcing function” of tasks, activities, or events that will drive the USDA to take action and produce a unified set of IT cost estimating activities and results

policy_statements.source_text: These practices, in conjunction with other investment-related knowledge, including work breakdown structures (WBS), schedules, risks, and lessons learned, will effectively inform USDA IT investment decision making.

This DR also supports the new IT budget authority provisions provided by the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, §831-837 (2014), which requires Federal Chief Information Officers (CIO) to fully define and understand the costs of agency IT investments, products, and services.
policy_statements.target: new IT budget authority provisions provided by the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, §831-837 (2014)
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, §831-837 (2014)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is effective immediately once published.
All USDA agencies and staff offices shall align their policies with this DR within 12 months of the published date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA agencies and staff offices
conditions: within 12 months of the published date

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with a July 11, 2012, Government Accountability Office (GAO) report, Information Technology Cost Estimation – Agencies Need to Address Significant Weaknesses in Policies and Practices, GAO-12-629, the GAO recommended that the Secretary of Agriculture, among other Agency or department heads listed in the report, “direct responsible officials to modify policies governing cost estimating to ensure that they address the weaknesses that we [GAO] identified.”
cross_references: Information Technology Cost Estimation – Agencies Need to Address Significant Weaknesses in Policies and Practices, GAO-12-629

policy_statements.source_text: To address this particular weakness, the USDA shall establish policies governing the use of IT cost estimating across the Department based on the GAO cost estimating guidelines and applied commensurate with the USDA investments size, cost, and scope.
policy_statements.target: policies governing the use of IT cost estimating across the Department
conditions: commensurate with the USDA investments size, cost, and scope

policy_statements.source_text: Developing and validating high-quality IT cost estimates, per the guidance and practices provided in the GAO Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide – Best Practices for Developing and Managing Capital Program Costs, GAO-09-3SP, March 2009, all meet the following characteristics:
cross_references: GAO Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide – Best Practices for Developing and Managing Capital Program Costs, GAO-09-3SP, March 2009

policy_statements.source_text: Credible: when assumptions and estimates are realistic.
conditions: when assumptions and estimates are realistic

policy_statements.source_text: The cost estimate has been cross-checked and reconciled with independent cost estimates, a level of confidence has been identified and a sensitivity analysis, as defined in GAO-09-3SP, has been conducted;

Well documented: maintain supporting documentation that includes a narrative explaining the process, sources, and methods used to create the IT cost estimate and identifies the underlying data and assumptions used to develop the IT cost estimate;
Accurate: when actual costs do not materially deviate from the assessment of costs likely to be incurred;
conditions: when actual costs do not materially deviate from the assessment of costs likely to be incurred

policy_statements.source_text: Comprehensive: when it accounts for all possible costs associated with an investment or project, is structured in sufficient detail to ensure that costs are neither omitted nor duplicated, and has been formulated by an estimating team with disciplines aligned with the investment’s development methodology; and
conditions: when it accounts for all possible costs associated with an investment or project, is structured in sufficient detail to ensure that costs are neither omitted nor duplicated, and has been formulated by an estimating team with disciplines aligned with the investment’s development methodology

policy_statements.source_text: Current: cost estimates must be updated at regular intervals or after events that impact the underlying assumptions of the estimate.
conditions: at regular intervals or after events that impact the underlying assumptions of the estimate

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA agencies and staff offices.
policy_statements.target: all USDA agencies and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA major IT investments, as defined in DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology (IT) Investments, and non-major IT investments, as defined in DR 3130-009, Non-Major Information Technology (IT) Investments, throughout their entire lifecycle, regardless of funding source, whether owned and operated by USDA, or operated on behalf of USDA.
conditions: whether owned and operated by USDA, or operated on behalf of USDA
cross_references: DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology (IT) Investments

policy_statements.source_text: Follow the 12-step GAO cost estimating approach presented in Figure 1 below (source: GAO-09-3SP, Chapter 1, Page 8, Figure 1) to capture the high-level business requirements that drive the need for a proposed technology solution; support the enterprise IT governance process; and minimize risk in the creation of high quality IT cost estimates.
policy_statements.target: 12-step GAO cost estimating approach presented in Figure 1 below

policy_statements.source_text: Tailor this 12-step GAO methodology for ease of Department-wide adoption into these five discrete steps:
Mission Need Identification: define the mission objectives, business needs, and the problem, gap, or issue that this IT investment, product, or service will resolve;
policy_statements.target: mission objectives, business needs, and the problem, gap, or issue that this IT investment, product, or service will resolve

policy_statements.source_text: Capability Definition: implementing a standard IT cost estimating process will provide for a meaningful comparison of capabilities between IT investment alternatives;
Solution Concept: design a solution concept that efficiently addresses business and technical capabilities;
policy_statements.target: solution concept that efficiently addresses business and technical capabilities

policy_statements.source_text: Cost/Benefit Estimation: justify the cost and benefit basis; and

Organizational Commitment – submit the results of the IT cost estimating analysis, including investment mission alignment, cost and benefit estimate, risk, and assumptions to the Associate Chief Information Officer (ACIO), Information Resource Management (IRM) for review and approval.
policy_statements.target: results of the IT cost estimating analysis, including investment mission alignment, cost and benefit estimate, risk, and assumptions

policy_statements.source_text: Implement the following practices and foundational criteria to enforce recommended cost analysis and estimating best practices to enable defensible IT investment proposals:

Clear requirements for cost estimating: account for incremental and/or full investment lifecycle costs that contribute to the probability of an investment’s success and potentially reduce budget and schedule overruns;
policy_statements.target: incremental and/or full investment lifecycle costs that contribute to the probability of an investment’s success and potentially reduce budget and schedule overruns

policy_statements.source_text: Compliance with cost estimating leading practices: require reviews of cost estimates for major IT investments to ensure they are reliable and defensible;
policy_statements.target: reviews of cost estimates for major IT investments

policy_statements.source_text: Process to collect and store cost-related data: develop a process to collect and store actual cost-related data from past estimates to support future estimates;
policy_statements.target: process to collect and store actual cost-related data from past estimates to support future estimates

policy_statements.source_text: Training: training in the cost estimation approach as presented in this DR will be offered to all personnel with program management and investment oversight responsibilities;
conditions: with program management and investment oversight responsibilities

policy_statements.source_text: Management review and approval: require the IT cost estimates be reviewed and submitted to the ACIO IRM before the annual IT portfolio reviews;
conditions: before the annual IT portfolio reviews

policy_statements.source_text: Develop a cost element structure (CES): require the use of a cost element structure (CES) to inform comprehensive cost and resource estimation for IT investments; and
policy_statements.target: use of a cost element structure (CES)

policy_statements.source_text: Provide cost estimating methods, tools, and templates: manage the methods, tools, and templates to maintain relevancy across the USDA for IT investment planning.

Agencies and staff offices may already have established cost estimating plans, techniques, and procedures based on their specific requirements and established methodologies, but all IT cost estimates should satisfy, at a minimum, the requirements addressed in this DR.
This DR adds additional controls without addressing the actual methodologies applied.
The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) shall:
Establish policies governing the use of cost estimating across the USDA, based on the GAO-09-3SP cost estimating guidelines;
policy_statements.target: policies governing the use of cost estimating across the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Establish, implement, and maintain an effective USDA IT cost estimating process with associated policies, guidance, tools, and training;
policy_statements.target: effective USDA IT cost estimating process with associated policies, guidance, tools, and training

policy_statements.source_text: Require that USDA IT investment cost estimates, as incorporated in the IT Portfolio (formerly the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Exhibit 53), be reviewed by the USDA Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Director, Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA) during the annual budget request, Passback, and monthly submissions to OMB;
conditions: during the annual budget request, Passback, and monthly submissions to OMB

policy_statements.source_text: Review cost estimates of IT-related costs in IT acquisitions;
policy_statements.target: cost estimates of IT-related costs in IT acquisitions

policy_statements.source_text: Establish an effective approach for developing high quality IT cost estimates that promotes informed decision making, realistic budget formulation, and meaningful progress measurement; and
policy_statements.target: effective approach for developing high quality IT cost estimates that promotes informed decision making, realistic budget formulation, and meaningful progress measurement

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct IT investment portfolio reviews with agencies and staff offices that include IT cost estimates developed from key principles and best practices addressed in this DR.
The USDA CFO shall:
Collaborate with the USDA CIO to confirm that the USDA IT Portfolio includes appropriate cost estimates of all IT resources included in budget requests prior to submission to OMB; and
Ensure IT acquisitions and procurements are supported by sound, reasonable IT cost estimates.
The Director, OBPA shall:
Collaborate with the USDA CIO and USDA CFO to affirm that the USDA IT Portfolio includes appropriate cost estimates of all IT resources included in budget requests prior to submission to OMB; and
Ensure IT acquisitions and procurements are supported by sound, reasonable IT cost estimates.
The ACIO IRM shall:
Ensure that agencies and staff offices are provided training opportunities in developing IT cost estimating based on key principles and best practices presented in this DR;
Provide IT cost estimating tools, guidelines, and templates to agencies and staff offices;
policy_statements.target: IT cost estimating tools, guidelines, and templates

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure IRM staff is available to assist agencies and staff offices with preparing IT cost estimates; and
Facilitate the annual IT investment portfolio reviews with agencies and staff offices that include IT cost estimates developed from key principles and best practices addressed in this DR.
The Director, Capital Planning and IT Governance Division (CPIGD) shall:
Assist agencies and staff offices with training and development of IT cost estimates;
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Capital Planning and IT Governance Division (CPIGD)

policy_statements.source_text: Provide IT cost estimating tools, guidelines, and templates to agencies and staff offices;
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Capital Planning and IT Governance Division (CPIGD)
policy_statements.target: IT cost estimating tools, guidelines, and templates

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure investment documentation outlines and provides supporting evidence of cost estimating based upon the key principles and best practices addressed in this DR;
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Capital Planning and IT Governance Division (CPIGD)

policy_statements.source_text: Assist agencies and staff offices with preparing IT cost estimates as part of the USDA Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) process as outlined in the USDA Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control Guide; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Capital Planning and IT Governance Division (CPIGD)
cross_references: USDA Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control Guide

policy_statements.source_text: Facilitate IT investment portfolio reviews with agencies and staff offices that includes IT cost estimates developed from key principles and best practices addressed in this DR.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Capital Planning and IT Governance Division (CPIGD)

policy_statements.source_text: Agency and staff office CIOs shall:
Provide IT cost estimates in accordance with key principles and best practices provided in this DR as part of the annual USDA IT portfolio review process conducted by the USDA CIO; and
conditions: as part of the annual USDA IT portfolio review process conducted by the USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Submit to the ACIO, IRM IT cost estimates supporting documentation for the USDA IT investment portfolio review and IT governance processes.
Agency and staff office IT Program/Project Managers shall:
Prepare IT cost estimates in accordance with the principles and best practices presented in this DR; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and staff office IT Program/Project Managers

policy_statements.source_text: Take advantage of training opportunities for IT cost estimating, as needed, and use any tools, guidelines, and templates provided by the ACIO, IRM.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and staff office IT Program/Project Managers
policy_statements.target: training opportunities for IT cost estimating

policy_statements.source_text: Procedures and operational practices applicable to this DR shall be further delineated in a Departmental Manual (DM) that will present detailed IT cost estimating processes and procedures.

a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy governing the use of information technology (IT) cost estimating key principles and uniform best practice guidance for all major and non-major USDA IT investments, projects, or systems. This DR incorporates leading practices that create a “forcing function” of tasks, activities, or events that will drive the USDA to take action and produce a unified set of IT cost estimating activities and results. These practices, in conjunction with other investment-related knowledge, including work breakdown structures (WBS), schedules, risks, and lessons learned, will effectively inform USDA IT investment decision making.
b. This DR also supports the new IT budget authority provisions provided by the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, §831-837 (2014), which requires Federal Chief Information Officers (CIO) to fully define and understand the costs of agency IT investments, products, and services.
extract_result.scope:

This DR incorporates leading practices that create a “forcing function” of tasks, activities, or events that will drive the USDA to take action and produce a unified set of IT cost estimating activities and results.
leading practices that create a “forcing function” of tasks, activities, or events that will drive the USDA to take action and produce a unified set of IT cost estimating activities and results

These practices, in conjunction with other investment-related knowledge, including work breakdown structures (WBS), schedules, risks, and lessons learned, will effectively inform USDA IT investment decision making.

This DR also supports the new IT budget authority provisions provided by the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act ( FITARA ), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, §831-837 (2014), which requires Federal Chief Information Officers (CIO) to fully define and understand the costs of agency IT investments, products, and services.

In accordance with a July 11, 2012, Government Accountability Office (GAO) report, *Information Technology Cost Estimation – Agencies Need to Address Significant Weaknesses in Policies and Practices*,  GAO-12-629 , the GAO recommended that the Secretary of Agriculture, among other Agency or department heads listed in the report, “direct responsible officials to modify policies governing cost estimating to ensure that they address the weaknesses that we [GAO] identified.” To address this particular weakness, the USDA shall establish policies governing the use of IT cost estimating across the Department based on the GAO cost estimating guidelines and applied commensurate with the USDA investments size, cost, and scope.

The cost estimate has been cross-checked and reconciled with independent cost estimates, a level of confidence has been identified and a sensitivity analysis, as defined in  GAO-09-3SP,  has been conducted;

Well documented: maintain supporting documentation that includes a narrative explaining the process, sources, and methods used to create the IT cost estimate and identifies the underlying data and assumptions used to develop the IT cost estimate;
Accurate: when actual costs do not materially deviate from the assessment of costs likely to be incurred;
when actual costs do not materially deviate from the assessment of costs likely to be incurred
